name: Pooltool Billiards
fullName: Pooltool billiards shot aiming: pot the target ball under legal-contact rules

actions.shoot: Submit one shot as a Speed level (Low=2, Medium=5, High=8 m/s V0) plus one of 9 Strikespots mapping to cue offsets (a,b); the harness sets phi via pt.aim.at_ball on the lowest-numbered ball and runs pt.simulate.

evaluation.efficiency: Report attempts used on success (lower is better), matching the published Average Attempts metric computed over successful episodes only, plus Pass@K for K up to 15.
evaluation.failure: Failure is exhausting 15 shots without potting the 9-ball, or reaching a state with no numbered balls left on the table while the 9-ball is unpotted. Unparseable actions consume a shot without simulating.
evaluation.success: The episode succeeds when a BALL_POCKET event for ball '9' occurs within the 15-shot budget, as adjudicated by the simulator.

assignment.generation: Instances are built with pt.get_rack(pt.GameType.NINEBALL, pt.Table.default()) under a recorded RNG seed; episode index 0..99 selects the seed, reproducing the official 100-experiment scale with a logged, replayable rack.
assignment.observation: Before each shot the agent receives the 2D top-down render of the current table state (ball positions and identities) plus the textual rules and action-space description. No privileged simulator state, event list or ground-truth trajectory is exposed.
assignment.reference: DeepPHY's Pooltool benchmark (arXiv:2508.05405, Appendix E) over Kiefl's Pooltool simulator: single-agent nine-ball where the goal is potting the 9-ball while each shot is auto-aimed at the lowest-numbered ball, with discrete Speed and Strikespot choices. New here: a fixed rack seed, retention of per-step observation images, and explicit episode-level scoring thresholds.
assignment.task: Starting from a Pooltool nine-ball rack, repeatedly strike the cue ball to pot the 9-ball. Every shot is automatically aimed at the lowest-numbered ball remaining, so the agent must choose power and spin that convert that forced contact into a legal pot.
assignment.verification: A run is valid when the per-episode JSON log records the seed, every shot's Speed/Strikespot and resolved (V0,a,b), the retained observation image, the simulator outcome label and potted-ball list, and the terminal is_solved flag, for both successful and failed episodes; replaying the seed and logged shots must reproduce the same outcome.

evaluation.allocationNote: 9 configurations x 3 planned repetitions; no runs performed; no success-rate screening.

notes: Environment logic is from the v3 engine and worker (src/h0-pooltool-isolated-v3.mjs, adapters/h0-pooltool-isolated-v3-engine.py and -worker.py): unchanged DeepPHY helper ASTs (04_pooltool_runner setup, cue reposition, potted-ball check; img_utils plot_static_pool_table), seeded nine-ball racks, Pooltool 0.4.4 simulation, observation text, stateHash digest and frame rendering.

Relocated: pooltool user configuration (CONFIG_DIR/PHYSICS_DIR) points at vendor/pooltool/configuration; only physics/resolver.yaml from pooltool-native-geoffrey-v3 is needed. Matplotlib and numba caches go to a per-episode temporary directory.

Observations contain publicText, terminal, stateHash, step and frame (media/<stateHash>.png, original top-down RGB). The per-episode instance field of the internal worker is not returned to the Player.
Player-facing actions: speed Low/Medium/High and one of nine strikespot names; the source runner auto-aims at the lowest-numbered remaining ball.

Train refresh lifecycle fix: wait for the Python process and stdio to close before removing its temporary HOME/caches; bounded cleanup retries handle delayed filesystem cleanup. Close-request errors remain errors. Native physics, actions and scoring are unchanged.
